title: Edmund and the Wreck
premise: Edmund Underhill is a salvage diver who has spent five years quietly working the Grey Wren, a wreck the navy forbids anyone to name, measuring his life in miles of rope and fathoms of cold water rather than years. When an upriver expedition led by salvage broker Beatrix Calloway stops answering its radio, Edmund is dragged into a race he never asked for: Beatrix's crew has found proof that the wreck was deliberately sunk to bury a crime, and the fleet that owns the river will kill to keep it that way. With six tides before the fleet's dredges arrive, Edmund must raise the evidence himself, choosing between loyalty to the harbor family that raised him and the truth that will destroy their livelihoods. In the end he surfaces the wreck's manifest at the flood tide, breaks the fleet's monopoly, and finds in Beatrix's ragged survivors the found family he never let himself want.
about_author: Tamsin Galloway is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent a decade working tidal waters before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people whose loyalties run deeper than the law allows.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A routine dive on the Grey Wren establishes his world: the tide charts, the harbor family who feed him, the navy buoy he's paid not to ask about. Emotional beat: comfortable isolation, a man who has stopped counting time.

chapters.title: The Radio Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Beatrix Calloway's expedition passes through buying dive gear, then her last transmission crackles over the harbor set — cut mid-word. The harbor master orders everyone to forget it. Beat: unease breaking through routine.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A fleet agent offers Edmund triple pay to guide their dredges upriver — and lets slip they expect 'trouble' already handled. Edmund realizes Beatrix may be alive. He refuses and starts planning. Beat: the first choice.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Owes
chapters.summary: Marisol, the harbor matriarch's daughter, POV. She begs Edmund not to go; the fleet owns their moorings. Their argument reveals the harbor family's debt to the fleet. Beat: loyalty as a chain.

chapters.title: Upriver in the Dark
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He slips past the fleet picket at slack water in a borrowed skiff. Near-miss with a patrol launch. Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Camp
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He finds the expedition camp flooded and ransacked, one tent slashed, a dive slate with half a message. Signs someone survived and went inland. Beat: dread.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He follows scratch marks to a drainage culvert and finds Beatrix, feverish, with a broken collarbone and a waterproof case she won't release. Beat: wary alliance begins.

chapters.title: The Case
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, flashback-tinged. She explains what her team found: the Grey Wren was scuttled in 1919 carrying a manifest proving the fleet's founders sank their own ship to defraud insurers and drown witnesses. Beat: the stakes become moral.

chapters.title: Tide Against Them
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Tide arithmetic: five tides left before the dredges arrive. They must move Beatrix downriver by boat despite her injuries. Beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: Old Friends, New Prices
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He buys passage from Danny Quill, an old diving partner, who warns him the fleet has posted a reward on 'the Calloway woman.' Beat: trust tested by money.

chapters.title: The Reward
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Danny wrestles with turning them in; his daughter needs surgery the fleet clinic would cover free. He lets them go but takes photos as insurance. Beat: compromise, not betrayal — yet.

chapters.title: Night on the Mudflats
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Grounded by low tide, they hide in the mud while a search launch sweeps its light overhead. Beatrix talks to keep him calm; he tells her about the wreck he's been diving for five years. Beat: intimacy forged under threat.

chapters.title: Why Edmund Dives
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, reflective. His brother died on a fleet job the company covered up; the harbor took Edmund in afterward. Now he understands why the Grey Wren matters personally. Beat: motive crystallizes into justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Dredges
chapters.summary: Fleet foreman Aldous Vane's POV. Vane learns Beatrix lives and dispatches the dredge early, four tides out. He is not a monster — he believes order requires the past stay buried. Beat: antagonist humanized, threat escalated.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She reveals the legal gambit: whoever raises the manifest first holds salvage rights, which would force public inquiry. The race isn't just escape — it's ownership of truth. Beat: plan formed.

chapters.title: Back to the Wreck
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They turn downriver toward the Grey Wren itself; Edmund must dive a site he's been paid to ignore. Three tides left. Beat: crossing the threshold.

chapters.title: The Navy Buoy
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A navy patrol boat questions them; Edmund uses his five years of quiet compliance as cover. The officer clearly knows more than he says. Beat: institutional complicity hinted.

chapters.title: Marisol's Choice
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The fleet pressures the harbor to report Edmund's position. Marisol burns the message instead, committing herself and the harbor to his side. Beat: loyalty tipping toward truth.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. First dive on the restricted section: bad visibility, snagged lines, and the hull breach that doesn't match any storm record. He finds the sealed strongroom door. Beat: awe and claustrophobia.

chapters.title: Two Tides
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Air and bottom time are short; the strongroom needs cutting gear they don't have. Beatrix improvises a plan using the expedition's abandoned explosives cache. Beat: desperation breeding ingenuity.

chapters.title: Danny Comes Back
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Haunted, Danny arrives with the cutting gear — and with the fleet's offer still ringing in his ears. He helps but won't say why yet. Beat: redemption offered, not sealed.

chapters.title: The Cut
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The charge goes off; Edmund enters the strongroom and finds the manifest, letters from drowned crew families, and a fleet founder's confession. Then his line parts in the surge. Beat: triumph turning to terror.

chapters.title: Lost Below
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, surface. Edmund misses his decompression window; Beatrix and Danny run the rescue against all practice. Beat: found family acting as one body.

chapters.title: Surfacing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Pulled up half-drowned, he clutches the manifest case. One tide remains. Beat: survival as grace, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: Vane Arrives
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The dredge reaches the wreck ahead of schedule. Vane offers Edmund everything — partnership, legitimacy, his brother's death officially acknowledged — if he hands over the case. Beat: temptation at full price.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund almost takes it; the acknowledgment of his brother is the thing he's wanted for five years. Beatrix doesn't argue — she just asks what his brother would have wanted surfaced. Beat: the dark night of the soul.

chapters.title: Harbor Rising
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Word spreads; harbor boats put out, not to fight but to form a wall between the dredge and Edmund's skiff. Ordinary people choosing sides. Beat: community as courage.

chapters.title: Last Tide
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The final tide turns; the channel will close behind them. They run the narrows with the dredge bearing down and the harbor wall of boats parting ahead. Beat: pure velocity.

chapters.title: Collision
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Vane's dredge clips the skiff; Danny takes the wheel and holds the line so Edmund and Beatrix can make shore, taking a crushing blow. Beat: sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Courthouse Steps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. On the quay, before assembled press and the navy officer from Chapter 17, Beatrix opens the case publicly. The confession, the manifest, the families' letters — read aloud. Beat: truth as a public act.

chapters.title: What the Law Does
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The fleet's lawyers descend; Vane disavows everything, offering Edmund immunity to testify only about piracy, not the sinking. Edmund must decide what justice he'll accept. Beat: the system's limits exposed.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the inquiry, Edmund testifies to all of it, burning his own salvage claim to do so — the manifest matters more than the money. Beat: principle over gain.

chapters.title: Vane's Fall
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The inquiry guts the fleet; Vane, offered scapegoat status by his own board, instead produces records implicating the founders' heirs. Ruin, chosen with dignity. Beat: antagonist's end.

chapters.title: Danny's Bill
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Recovering, Danny finally explains: his brother was one of the 1919 crew. The surgery gets paid by the crews' descendants' fund. Beat: debts settled across a century.

chapters.title: Salvage
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The Grey Wren is raised properly, respectfully; the crew's names are read at the quayside. Edmund dives the empty hull one last time and lets his brother's ghost rest. Beat: grief resolved.

chapters.title: Anchorage
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix, healed, offers Edmund a place on a new honest survey outfit. He hesitates — harbors are hard to leave. Beat: the invitation to belong.

chapters.title: Miles Become Years
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund stops measuring life in miles; the harbor throws no party, just sets another plate. Marisol teases him about staying. Beat: warmth without sentimentality.

chapters.title: The New Chart
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating brief POVs. Months later: the river re-charted, the fleet dissolved into cooperatives, the navy buoy removed. Each character sees the changed water differently. Beat: the world remade.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund and Beatrix dive a harmless, lovely wreck together for no reason but wonder. He gives her his father's compass; she gives him the expedition's flag. Beat: love declared in objects, not words.

chapters.title: Flood Tide
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, closing. Standing at the harbor mouth at full flood, Edmund reflects that truth, like tide, always comes back — you only have to be there when it does. He turns toward home, and stays. Beat: resolution, peace earned.
